Born at Pomfret, Connecticut, on 1 April 1770, son of Thomas Hutchins and Priscilla Dana.
Part of the post-Revolution New England exodus north: by the family book, he and Betsey went from Weathersfield,
on the Connecticut River in Vermont, to Eden, in the north of the state, after 1800 (his sister Jane
was born at Weathersfield in 1792 and married at Belvidere, near Eden, in 1812: Dodge Genealogy, 1894)
, and they settled at Constable in Franklin County, New York, in 1808 by one history or during the War of 1812 by
another. The family book tells how they came: across Lake Champlain on the ice,
with their children, Cyril’s brother Ebenezer and Jedediah Hastings, the horses slipping until sacking was tied over
their hoofs. At Constable Cyril farmed, and he and his sons built a tavern.
He died on 1 December 1834. Betsey, a niece of Ethan Allen by the family book, outlived him by 28 years.
